title: telemetry-tempered-ab-orchestrator-with-smoke-rail-slow-start-and-auto-rollforward-playbook
author: Priya Sharma
description: Motivation: Managing A/B experiments and canaries at scale requires fast, actionable telemetry decisions that minimize false positives while avoiding slow rollbacks. This PR introduces a telemetry-tempered A/B orchestrator that imposes a slow-start smoke rail and uses derivative-based metric detectors to decide auto-rollforwards and automated rollbacks. Design summary: single control-plane operator that coordinates per-slice A/B allocation, a short 'smoke rail' phase for lightweight Canary validation, and an adaptive slow-start that exponentially grows traffic only when both level and derivative metrics are stable. The operator applies three tiers of safety gates: unit smoke checks (syntactic / smoke-level), stability windows (statistical-level checks across moving windows), and derivative monitors that detect sudden trend changes. Auto-rollforward: when the derivative remains positive for a configured window and absolute metrics meet SLO thresholds, traffic expands automatically using a bounded growth schedule. Auto-rollback: if derivative crosses negative thresholds or loss of fidelity on golden prompts is detected, the operator triggers a quarantine lane and automatic rollback with snapshot playback. Changes included: 1) orchestration controller implementing phased slow-start and smoke rails, 2) new telemetry policy DSL for defining derivative thresholds and smoke sets, 3) replayable snapshot checkpointing for safe rollback and bisect, 4) small console UX to visualize smoke-phase signals and allow manual aborts, 5) unit and integration tests plus a canary on the perf lab. Checklist: - [x] Controller core logic implemented - [x] Telemetry DSL parser and validation - [x] Snapshot checkpointing + replay hook - [x] Console visualization & controls - [x] Unit tests (controller, policy parsing) - [x] Integration tests with perf-canary harness - [x] Documentation and changelog entry Rollout plan: staged rollout to internal staging, smoke runs against perf-canary for 48h, after passing roll out to 10% of production traffic for 6h with monitoring, then step to 50% if stable. Migration notes: backward compatible with existing rollout policies; default slow-start disabled unless policy uses new DSL. Testing notes: perf-canary run shows 3x faster abort detection for injected regressions and no false aborts in baseline evaluation. Related work items: ENG-4128 (quarantine lanes), PM-188 (AB UX requirements).

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Important improvement. Two questions: how does the derivative detector behave with sparse events (e.g. low qps)? Please add a jitter guard to growth schedule.
Priya Sharma (author): Added a jitter cap and a low-qps debounce in detectors; see derivative.go lines 42-78. Updated tests to cover low-qps behavior.
Hannah Lee: Can we make the smoke rail dataset configurable per-tenant? Some enterprise customers have stricter golden prompts.

release_notes: Introduces a telemetry-tempered A/B orchestrator with slow-start smoke rails, derivative-based auto-rollforward and auto-rollback, per-namespace smoke set config, and snapshot-based rollback/replay. Backward compatible by default; to opt-in, use the new rollout DSL described in docs/rollouts/telemetry_tempered_orchestrator.md.
notes_for_ops: Enable operator by default in staging clusters. For production enablement, add RBAC for snapshot-store and configure smoke sets. Default policy disables auto-expansion unless explicitly enabled in rollout DSL.
